pharm: A calcium sensitiser that increases myocardial contractility without raising intracellular calcium and opens ATP-sensitive potassium channels to cause vasodilation; used IV for acute decompensated heart failure (not FDA-approved)

Avoid breastfeeding during and for some days after (long-acting metabolite)

Not relevant to acute IV use
Continuous ECG, blood pressure, heart rate, potassium, fluid status
summary: Levosimendan is an intravenous calcium-sensitising inodilator used for the short-term treatment of acute decompensated severe chronic heart failure where conventional therapy is insufficient and inotropic support is appropriate. It increases cardiac contractility by sensitising cardiac troponin C to calcium without increasing intracellular calcium or myocardial oxygen demand, and causes arterial and venous vasodilation by opening ATP-sensitive potassium channels. The usual regimen is an optional loading dose of 6-12 mcg/kg over 10 minutes followed by a continuous infusion of 0.05-0.2 mcg/kg/min, typically for up to 24 hours; a lower loading dose is used if there is risk of hypotension. It has a long-acting metabolite (OR-1896) that prolongs its haemodynamic effect for days after the infusion ends. Common adverse effects are hypotension, headache and tachyarrhythmias, and hypokalaemia should be corrected before use. Levosimendan is NOT FDA-approved; it is licensed in many other countries, and dosing follows the SmPC/EMA-region prescribing information.
indications: Short-term treatment of acute decompensated severe chronic heart failure (ADHF) in situations where conventional therapy is not sufficient and inotropic support is considered appropriate
(Used in some settings perioperatively for low cardiac output - per local practice, not a universal label indication)

dosage.t: IV via infusion pump; assess response over the first 30-60 min
dosage.n: Use the lower loading dose (6 mcg/kg) if concomitant vasodilators/risk of hypotension

dosage.t: Continuous IV infusion, usually total duration about 24 hours
dosage.n: Effects persist for days due to active metabolite OR-1896

admin: For intravenous use only; administer the diluted solution by infusion pump in a setting with continuous cardiac monitoring
Correct hypovolaemia and hypokalaemia before starting
Use an optional loading dose over 10 minutes, then a continuous maintenance infusion, typically for up to 24 hours
Monitor blood pressure and ECG continuously; reduce or stop the infusion for significant hypotension or tachyarrhythmia
Be aware that haemodynamic effects persist for several days after stopping because of the active metabolite
Do not initiate in severe hypotension/tachycardia, severe outflow obstruction or severe renal/hepatic impairment
moa: Levosimendan exerts a dual mechanism. As a calcium sensitiser it binds calcium-saturated cardiac troponin C in a calcium-dependent manner, stabilising the troponin conformation and enhancing the force of contraction without increasing intracellular calcium concentration or myocardial oxygen consumption - so contractility improves without the arrhythmogenic and energetic costs of classical inotropes. It also opens ATP-sensitive potassium channels in vascular smooth muscle (and mitochondria), producing arterial and venous vasodilation that reduces preload and afterload, and conferring possible cardioprotective effects. Its active metabolite OR-1896 has similar actions and a long half-life, extending the haemodynamic effect for days.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to levosimendan or excipients
Significant mechanical obstruction affecting ventricular filling or outflow (or both)
relative: Low baseline blood pressure or risk of hypotension
Hypokalaemia or other electrolyte disturbance (correct first)
Tachyarrhythmias / atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
Ischaemic heart disease with ongoing ischaemia

preg: There are no adequate data on use in pregnant women, and animal data have shown reproductive toxicity. Levosimendan should be avoided in pregnancy and used only if the potential benefit clearly outweighs the risk.
lact: Levosimendan and its long-acting metabolite may be present in milk; breastfeeding should be avoided during treatment and for several days afterwards because of the prolonged metabolite half-life.
renal: Use with caution in mild-to-moderate renal impairment, as the active metabolite (OR-1896) may accumulate and prolong haemodynamic effects. It is contraindicated in severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance below about 30 mL/min).
hepatic: Use with caution in mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment; it is contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment because of altered metabolism and elimination.

major: Other vasodilators / antihypertensives - additive, potentially severe hypotension
Other IV inotropes and QT-prolonging drugs - additive arrhythmia and QT-prolongation risk
moderate: Drugs causing hypokalaemia (diuretics) - increase arrhythmia risk; correct potassium first
Beta-blockers - the inotropic effect of levosimendan is not blunted by beta-blockade (unlike classical inotropes), but combined haemodynamic effects need monitoring
minor: Mild additive effects with other rate/rhythm-active agents
interactions.alcohol: Not relevant to acute IV use
interactions.diagnostics: Can prolong the QT interval and lower serum potassium; monitor ECG and electrolytes

serious: Ventricular tachycardia, atrial fibrillation with rapid response
QT-interval prolongation with risk of torsades de pointes
emergency: Sustained ventricular tachyarrhythmia / torsades de pointes

monitoring: Continuous ECG monitoring (rhythm and QT interval) during and after the infusion
Blood pressure and heart rate frequently during titration
Serum potassium and other electrolytes (correct before and during)
Fluid balance and signs of hypovolaemia
Ongoing haemodynamic monitoring for several days given the long-acting metabolite
counsel: This is a heart-support drip given in hospital under close heart and blood-pressure monitoring
Its benefit can last several days after the drip finishes because it forms a long-lasting active substance in the body
Tell staff at once if you feel faint, dizzy, have palpitations or chest pain
Blood tests (especially potassium) will be checked before and during treatment
It is avoided in pregnancy and breastfeeding and in severe kidney or liver problems
pk: Haemodynamic effect within minutes of the loading dose/start of infusion
Effect peaks during the infusion; metabolite effect peaks after the infusion ends
Parent drug about 1 hour; active metabolite OR-1896 about 75-80 hours
Haemodynamic effects persist for up to 7-9 days after a 24-hour infusion (metabolite)
Store concentrate refrigerated (2-8 C), protect from light; use the diluted infusion within the time stated in the SmPC
pearls: NOT FDA-approved; licensed in many other countries (e.g. EU, India) - dosing follows the SmPC (loading 6-12 mcg/kg then 0.05-0.2 mcg/kg/min, usually 24 h)
Calcium sensitiser: improves contractility without raising myocardial oxygen demand and without losing effect under beta-blockade
Long-acting active metabolite (OR-1896, t1/2 ~75-80 h) means haemodynamic effects persist for up to a week after a 24-hour infusion
Correct hypokalaemia and hypovolaemia before use; watch for hypotension and tachyarrhythmias/QT prolongation
Contraindicated in severe hypotension, severe renal (CrCl <30) or severe hepatic impairment, and a history of torsades
missed: Not applicable - levosimendan is given as a clinician-controlled IV infusion in a monitored setting, not as scheduled self-administered doses.
overdose: Overdose produces exaggerated effects: marked hypotension and tachycardia, and these may persist because of the long-acting metabolite. Management is supportive with continuous cardiovascular monitoring: stop or reduce the infusion, give IV fluids and vasopressors/inotropes for hypotension, and treat arrhythmias; effects may take days to resolve.
